prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Tailscale's free Personal plan (users, devices, other limits). Cite Tailscale's own pricing or documentation page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on Tailscale's official pricing and documentation pages, here are the documented limits for their free Personal plan:

The free Personal plan allows for up to 6 users in a single tailnet (Tailscale network). [tailscale.com](https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal) | QUOTE: "Up to 6 users" | CLAIM: Personal plan has a 6-user limit
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/docs/account/manage-plans/free-plans-discounts | QUOTE: "The Personal plan permits 6 free users in a single Tailscale network" | CLAIM: Personal plan allows 6 users in one tailnet

User devices (computers, phones, etc.) are unlimited on all plans, including the free Personal plan.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "Unlimited user devices" | CLAIM: No limit on user devices
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "User Devices Computers, phones, etc. | Unlimited" | CLAIM: User devices have no quantity limit

The plan includes up to 50 tagged resources (servers, exit nodes, subnet routers, etc.) at no cost.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "Up to 50 tagged resources to start" | CLAIM: 50 tagged resources included
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "50 tagged resources included" | CLAIM: Base allocation of 50 tagged resources

The plan provides 1,000 minutes per month for ephemeral resources (short-lived workloads like CI/CD runners, Kubernetes pods).
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "1,000 mins per month for ephemeral resources" | CLAIM: 1,000 minute monthly allowance for ephemeral resources
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Ephemeral resources Short-running k8s pods, CI/CD runners, etc. | 1,000 mins per month" | CLAIM: 1,000 minutes monthly ephemeral resource pool

Access Control List (ACL) groups are limited to 3 groups.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "Up to 3 ACL groups" | CLAIM: Maximum of 3 ACL groups
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "ACL Groups | 3" | CLAIM: ACL groups limited to 3

The Personal plan provides access to nearly all of Tailscale's features, including the ability to try SSH and Kubernetes features.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "Access nearly all of Tailscale's features" | CLAIM: Most features are available
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "Try SSH and Kubernetes features" | CLAIM: SSH and Kubernetes features available for trial

It's worth noting that according to their documentation, Tailscale is currently not enforcing hard limits or overages for ACL groups, multiple tailnets, tagged resources, and ephemeral resources.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing?plan=personal | QUOTE: "we are currently not enforcing the hard limits or overages of ACL groups, multiple tailnets, tagged resources, and ephemeral resources" | CLAIM: Some limits are not currently being enforced
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "we are currently not enforcing the hard limits or overages of ACL groups, multiple tailnets, tagged resources, and ephemeral resources" | CLAIM: Temporary non-enforcement of certain limits

NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Whether there are any bandwidth or data transfer limits on the Personal plan
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Whether there are any limitations on the number of simultaneous connections
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: Whether there are any geographic restrictions on usage
